profile.reading:
This building is addressed 5200 Rogers Road in San Antonio's Westover Hills district, the area where Microsoft opened its first two San Antonio data centers in 2015 at roughly $90 million each. That original investment grew into a much larger regional footprint: by August 2023 Microsoft operated at least eight data centers across Bexar and Medina counties with cumulative investment exceeding $1.2 billion, per San Antonio Report reporting. San Antonio's city council approved a 15-year Chapter 380 tax reimbursement in 2013 covering 40% of property taxes in exchange for a $250 million Microsoft investment commitment and the creation of 20 high-paying jobs, an incentive package the company has since built well beyond. Named Westover Hills-area buildings identified in local reporting include SAT14 on nearby Wiseman Boulevard, a 411,000-square-foot complex Microsoft has continued expanding through 2024. Construction phases at Microsoft's San Antonio campuses have typically employed several hundred workers, while completed data center buildings tend to run with a comparatively small operating staff of roughly 50 employees once online. Microsoft has not published this specific Rogers Road building's square footage or MW capacity, so this registry records the SAT14 figure as regional context rather than a confirmed fact for this exact structure.

CPS Energy, San Antonio's municipally owned electric and gas utility, the largest such public utility in the country, supplies power to Microsoft's San Antonio-area campuses and has cited large commercial and industrial customers, data centers among them, in its own integrated resource planning as it weighs new generation to meet growing demand. Because CPS Energy is municipally owned rather than investor-owned, large-load agreements with customers like Microsoft are negotiated directly with the city-owned utility rather than through the Public Utility Commission of Texas process that governs most of the state's investor-owned utilities.

reading.body:
Microsoft opened its first two San Antonio data centers in the Westover Hills district in 2015, each costing roughly $90 million. The original facility at 5200 Rogers Road was part of that initial wave, though this specific building's square footage and power capacity are not published. By August 2023, Microsoft's San Antonio-region footprint had grown to at least eight facilities across Bexar and Medina counties with cumulative investment exceeding $1.2 billion, built under a 15-year property tax incentive approved by San Antonio city council in 2013.

The individual power capacity of the Rogers Road building is not published by Microsoft. A nearby named facility in the Westover Hills area, SAT14 on Wiseman Boulevard, occupies 411,000 square feet and has remained under active expansion through 2024, but that figure cannot be attributed to the Rogers Road address without confirmation. Because this site has mapped 133 facilities across Texas but only 18 have published power specifications totaling 468 MW, most data centers in the state operate without disclosed capacity figures.

San Antonio's power comes from CPS Energy, a municipally owned utility that is the largest public utility of its kind in the country. CPS Energy has named data centers among the large commercial loads driving its integrated resource planning for new generation capacity. Because CPS Energy is municipally owned rather than regulated by the Public Utility Commission of Texas, power agreements with major customers like Microsoft are negotiated directly with the city rather than through the investor-owned utility process that governs most of Texas. The binding constraint on Microsoft's expansion in San Antonio is therefore negotiation with one city-owned utility rather than coordination across the fragmented grid that covers the rest of the state.
